 Dame Prue Leith makes heartbreaking admission about life after husband's death
 Her first husband died in 2002
 Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:47, 14 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Dame Prue Leith made an honest admission over friendship (Image: Channel 4) 
 Dame Prue Leith has opened up about what she describes as one of the biggest regrets of her life - admitting that her attitude towards friendships left her feeling "lonely" following the death of her first husband.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 The 86-year-old television personality has enjoyed a long and successful career as a chef, restaurateur, author and broadcaster. However, despite her achievements, Prue has revealed that there is one thing she wishes she had approached differently.
 ‌ 
 Speaking candidly about her personal life, the former Great British Bake Off judge admitted that she had not always placed enough importance on maintaining friendships, something she later came to regret.
 Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter 
 In an interview with the Daily Mail, Prue confessed: "I've been very bad at friendship. I never thought it was important. If someone had said, 'You don't have any friends,' I'd have said, 'What do we need friends for?' It didn't occur to me it was unwise."
 She went on to describe her attitude towards friendships as "one of the only regrets" she has had throughout her life. The TV star explained that the consequences became particularly apparent after her first husband, property developer Rayne Kruger, died in 2002.
 ‌ 
 Prue realised she had not built the close friendships that could have offered support during such a difficult period. She admitted that she did not even know her neighbours at the time, leaving her feeling particularly isolated. She has since found happiness again with her second husband, John Playfair, whom she met in 2010. Prue has previously praised John for being much better at maintaining friendships and bringing people together at their home in the Cotswolds.
 View 2 Images She announced her Bake Off departure this year (Image: Instagram) 
 ‌ 
 Her latest admission comes after Prue opened up about another significant decision in her life, her departure from The Great British Bake Off after almost nine years as a judge. Having joined the Channel 4 programme in 2017 following Mary Berry's exit, she became a familiar face alongside Paul Hollywood.
 To get the very latest television and celebrity news in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source 
 ‌ 
 Speaking to Woman Magazine about her decision to leave, Prue admitted that she had started thinking more about how she wanted to spend her remaining years, particularly when it came to enjoying the summer months.
 She said: "You can't be 86 without thinking about death a bit. I realised that I would never have a summer holiday in Europe again. Two years ago, I told them I was going to leave and they asked why and I said because I want a holiday in the summer."
 ‌ 
 Prue is also preparing to return to television with a new travel series alongside her former Bake Off colleague Sandi Toksvig. Prue & Sandi's South African Adventure will see the pair explore Prue's native South Africa and is due to air on Channel 4 later this month.
 Speaking about her exit at the time, she said: "Bake Off has been a fabulous part of my life for the last nine years, I have genuinely loved it and I’m sure I’ll miss working with my fellow judge Paul, Alison and Noel and the teams at Love Productions and Channel 4.
 Article continues below "But now feels like the right time to step back (I’m 86 for goodness sake!), there’s so much I’d like to do, not least spend summers enjoying my garden. Whoever joins the team, I’m sure they’ll love it as much as I have. I feel very lucky to have been part of it."
